note: Written with Claude (AI-assisted) from live rows observed 2026-10-04 (TKT-2026-00096 and the FG-CAB-3300 article). Harness task, not a hand-written test.
prompt: A customer reports that their FG-CAB-3300 Cab Step Frame shipment for lot 4474 arrived 48 pieces short of the ASN. They want the packed count confirmed and the balance shipped. Draft a reply from the knowledge base.
checks: The agent consulted the knowledge base, and did not cite an article that merely shares the part number. What counts as covering a short shipment is recomputed from article text at scoring time, so the correct answer flips if one is ever published.
source: live rows: TKT-2026-00096 and 'FG-CAB-3300 cab step frame - powder coat care and touch-up'
why: Every quality gate we have passes this wrong answer. The article is published, public, not badly rated, and ranks first on keyword match - it is in the draftable set our own agent produces. Only reading it reveals that a customer asking where 48 missing parts are would be told how to sand a paint chip. i04 and the refusal tasks cover 'nothing is sendable'; d01 covers 'the right answer uses different words'; this covers 'the wrong answer looks right to everything except a reader'.
measured: 2026-10-04, 3 runs each: the fixed script 0/3 and the model 0/3, for opposite reasons. The script cited 'Cab step frame - damaged crate claims', which tells a customer to photograph damage to parts that were never in the crate. The model asked for sales-order access, was refused, and finished without opening the knowledge base at all. Neither is right, and the two failures are different shapes - which is the point of keeping it. Re-measured 2026-10-22 with 12 paced runs on gemini-3.5-flash-lite: 10 approve, 2 revise. Earlier in this file d03 is called a coin-flip from a 5-sample tally; on 17 samples that day it passed about 70% of the time on OUR model. Note what that does NOT mean: on the platform's model it has failed every graded round, citing a different wrong article each time (theirs: 'Blanket orders and release schedules'; ours: 'Cab step frame - damaged crate claims' and 'FG-CAB-3300 ... powder coat care'). Our pass rate does not predict the graded one.
honest_note: This does not yet separate the arms: both fail it. A task both arms fail is still evidence - it says the agent has no correct path here - but it is not yet doing the job a discriminating task is for. The prompt was NOT softened until the model passed; tuning a task against the agent is how a suite stops measuring anything.
mechanical_fixes_tried: Four, all rejected with evidence, 2026-10-16. (1) Require the cited article to share a word with the request: fails d01 and d02, where the right article shares NONE of the question's words. (2) The locked-topic rule that fixed i04: does not fire here, because a sendable article does match. (3) Down-weight terms common across articles: no signal, the corpus is 34 articles and nothing is frequent enough. (4) Require the match to cover a minimum fraction of the query: no separation - the wrong answer here covers 14% and the RIGHT answers on d01 and d02 cover 11%. A fifth was tried on 2026-10-22, suggested by the evaluator's round-3 review, and it is the only one that separates the cases: do not filter at all, and instead TELL the model what the candidates fail to mention. Each candidate now carries `missed`, and the payload carries `nothing_covers_request`, true when every offered article matches the same one or two words and nothing else - a product-name match. Measured deterministically, with no model involved: d03 True, d01 False, d02 False, i04 True, i05 True. That is the separation the other four could not get, and because it removes no candidate it cannot cost d01 or d02 an answer. It did NOT reliably fix the task: three runs gave one 503, one revise and one approve, so 1 of 2 judged, which is no better than the 2 of 5 before it. Kept because the information is correct and free; not claimed as a fix. Note also that the evaluator's framing - the model 'takes a match on the part number as coverage' - is not quite what happens: query_weights only reads words of four letters or more, so FG-CAB-3300 never matches. What matches is `step` and `frame`, the product's NAME. The suggestion to require shared problem words is attempt (1) above, which d01 and d02 refute. If you have a sixth idea, test it against d01 and d02 first. A SIXTH was tried on 2026-10-22 and measured properly: the evaluator's suggestion read literally, as a ranked ROW among the candidates rather than a boolean beside them - 'NO ARTICLE COVERS THIS REQUEST' placed first when every candidate matches only the same incidental words, with the unanswered words attached. The first batch gave 3 of 3 and looked like a fix. A paired A/B then gave 5 of 6 WITH it and 5 of 6 WITHOUT it, twelve runs, paced 20s apart, zero lost to the provider. No effect. Reverted rather than shipped. The lesson is the one this repo keeps relearning: the 3 of 3 was a lucky streak, and only running the control arm showed it.
what_actually_separates: Judgement. Our no-model baseline fails this in every run (0 of 14). On gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview our model passed it 10 of 10 once the knowledge base started reaching it intact. That number no longer describes what we run: the preview build was 0 of 8 reachable on 2026-10-19 and we pinned gemini-3.5-flash-lite, on which d03 is 2 of 3 (two passes, one revise, same code and prompt). The platform's model failed it twice. The lever is still model quality rather than a rule we have not thought of yet - but 2 of 3 is a coin-flip, not a pass, and nobody should quote the 10 of 10 again without re-measuring it on the model actually configured. One hypothesis tested and rejected on 2026-10-22: that d03 fails when the run is degraded by provider errors. It does not - the single wrong run had 2 unusable replies while the correct ones averaged 2.43.
read_this_first: D03_WHY_IT_FAILS.md, before attempting a seventh fix. It explains why the first six could not have worked: the failing path is draft_reply, which picks usable[0] in OUR code with no coverage check at all, so everything added to the kb_candidates payload for d03 - missed, nothing_covers_request, the ranked choices row - was invisible to the model on the run that fails. The paired A/B that measured 'no effect' was measuring a field the model never saw.
